title: Poached Pear Frangipane Tart
summary: A crisp sweet pastry case filled with almond frangipane and fanned poached pear halves, glazed with apricot.

ingredients.note: the syrup is not eaten; about 30 g of its sugar is counted

ingredients.item: lemon juice, plus 3 strips of peel
firm, just-ripe pears (about 800 g), peeled, halved and cored
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: bring the water, sugar, lemon juice and peel and vanilla to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pear halves, cover with a circle of baking paper and simmer gently 12-18 min until a knife slides in easily. Cool in the syrup, then drain on kitchen paper. Gentle simmering softens the pears without breaking them.

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: beat the yolk with the cream. Pulse the flour, icing sugar and salt, add the butter and pulse to coarse crumbs, then add the yolk mix and pulse until it just clumps. Press into a disc, wrap and chill 1 h.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: roll to 3 mm, line the tin and freeze 20 min. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) with the tray inside. Line with paper and beans and bake 20 min, then uncovered 5-8 min until dry and pale golden. Lower the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).

steps.title: Frangipane
steps.text: beat the butter and sugar until pale, 3 min. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the ground almonds, flour, almond flavouring and salt until smooth. Spread evenly in the case.

steps.title: Pears
steps.text: slice each pear half crosswise into thin slices, keeping its shape, then press gently to fan it. Lift each half on the palette knife and set them on the frangipane like spokes, narrow ends to the centre.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake 40-45 min until the frangipane is puffed, golden and springs back, and a skewer comes out clean. Warm the jam with the water, sieve and brush over the pears. Cool at least 1 h before slicing. The frangipane rises round the pears and holds them in place.

tips: A common mistake is using wet pears; pat them dry so juice does not make the frangipane soggy.
Poach the pears up to 2 days ahead and keep them in their syrup in the fridge.
Use pears that are firm, as very ripe ones turn to mush.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days; bring to room temperature before serving.
